entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv5168"/><div sID="gen7694" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv5168"/>8. Elihu claims inspiration, as a divinely commissioned messenger to Job (<reference osisRef="Job.33.6">Job 33:6</reference>, <reference osisRef="Job.33.23">23</reference>); and that claim is not contradicted in <reference osisRef="Job.42.4">Job 42:4</reference>, <reference osisRef="Job.42.5">5</reference>. Translate: "But the spirit (which God puts) in man, and the inspiration ... is that which giveth," &c.; it is not mere "years" which give understanding (<reference osisRef="Prov.2.6">Pr 2:6</reference>; <reference osisRef="John.20.22">Joh 20:22</reference>). <div eID="gen7694" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv5172"/><div sID="gen7702" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv5172"/>13. This has been so ordered, "lest you should" pride yourselves on having overcome him by your "wisdom" (<reference osisRef="Jer.9.23">Jr 9:23</reference>, the great aim of the Book of Job); and that you may see, "God alone can thrust him down," that is, confute him, "not man." So Elihu grounds his confutation, not on the maxims of sages, as the friends did, but on his special commission from God (<reference osisRef="Job.32.8">Job 32:8</reference>; <reference osisRef="Job.33.4">33:4</reference>, <reference osisRef="Job.33.6">6</reference>). <div eID="gen7702" type="x-p"/>

So Elihu grounds his confutation, not on the maxims of sages, as the friends did, but on his special commission from God ( Job 32:8 ; 33:4 , 6 ).

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv5177"/><div sID="gen7710" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv5177"/><hi type="bold">19. belly--</hi>bosom: from which the words of Orientalists in speaking seem to come more than with us; they speak gutturally. "Like (new) wine (in fermentation) without a vent," to work itself off. New wine is kept in new goatskin bottles. This fittingly applies to the young Elihu, as contrasted with the old friends (<reference osisRef="Matt.9.7">Mt 9:7</reference>). <div eID="gen7710" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv5179"/><div sID="gen7712" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv5179"/>21. "May I never accept," &c. Elihu alludes to Job's words (<reference osisRef="Job.13.8">Job 13:8</reference>, <reference osisRef="Job.13.10">10</reference>), wherein he complains that the friends plead for God partially, "accepting His person." Elihu says he will not do so, but will act impartially between God and Job. "And I will not give flattery," &c. (<reference osisRef="Prov.24.23">Pr 24:23</reference>). <div eID="gen7712" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: 21. "May I never accept," &c. Elihu alludes to Job's words ( Job 13:8 , 10 ), wherein he complains that the friends plead for God partially, "accepting His person."
